brief: The Market Ear frames the SPX rebound since the November 5 AI-driven selloff as a short squeeze, not fresh conviction buying, and warns it may still be a bear-market trap. SPX is back near the middle of its range and above its 200-day moving average; NDX bounced off a trendline but stays below its 200-day MA. Goldman says S&P futures open interest jumped $19.1bn on November 5, the fifth-largest daily rise in two years, as investors added shorts, then fell $16.6bn as the S&P rallied 2.7% through November 9, implying short covering drove the move. UBS puts CTA global equity exposure at -5%, the 5th percentile over one year, down from +150% at the cycle peak, leaving room to rebuild if markets extend higher; vol-control funds that cut exposure as volatility spiked (Nomura) could also become buyers if realized volatility falls, and Nomura's Privorotsky calls positioning a tailwind against a rising-yield headwind. Goldman ties the rebound's durability to semiconductors, which fell 12.2% on November 5 and dragged the S&P down 4.4%. BTIG's Krinsky finds that across eight historical 10%+ crash/5%+ rebound episodes, none marked a lasting bottom, with seven losing about 10% over the next 30 days. BTIG stays bearish on SOXX below $165, targeting $115-120.
